name: Jonas Pennywhistle
title: inventor of the second spoon
examine: Jonas Pennywhistle holds a spoon in each hand and has not been seen to eat. The second is always more polished.
A neat sign on his satchel reads ALSO. Nobody has asked him what it means.
He stops to look at every spoon he passes, and every ladle. He seems to disapprove of the ladles.
meet: You’ll have noticed the spoon in my left hand, and the spoon in my right.
Jonas Pennywhistle. I invented the second one.

wary: A spoon is a serious matter. Two is a serious matter twice.
neutral: Welcome back. Mind the satchel. There is a soup in it somewhere.
warm: Ah. A friend. I was about to be right about something. Stay.
fond: Just the person. I’ve been saving the best spoon for you, which is to say, the second.

tired: I’ve nothing left but spoons, and I’ve said everything about those. I won’t say it again today.
finished: That’s the lot. I could say it again. I would say it exactly the same.

say: The first spoon is a fine spoon. Nobody disputes that. But what do you do with it when your hands are full? You pick up the second. I invented that.

options.text: How is the second spoon different from the first?
reply: People expect more. There isn’t more.

options.text: Does it get to be first on Tuesdays?
reply: You have understood the entire problem.

options.text: I think the first spoon already had a second.
reply: There was a fork. That doesn’t count.

say: I filed for the second spoon. The clerk asked, second to what? I said, the first. He said, then it’s a spoon. I said, a second spoon. We were there until dusk.

reply: Four. And a sketch of a soup.
“ALSO”. Yes. It’s on the form. I have it framed.

options.text: Clerks are right more often than inventors.
reply: That is a very general claim.
You’re kind. You would drop the spoons.

say: People ask about a third spoon. I tell them not to be greedy.

options.text: What if the third is a ladle?
reply: A ladle is a large spoon. I had never thought of it.
Luck doesn’t live in a spoon. Third time, though.
Somebody had to not ask for it first.

say: I would like to test the second spoon on a soup hot enough to deserve it. Do you know of one?

reply: It’s a date. I will write it on the spoon.
That doesn’t help the soup. But thank you.

errand.title: A soup hot enough
offer: The second spoon has never been used. It needs a soup that deserves it.
Cook a minnow supper at your fire. I’ll know. A spoon knows.

steps.text: Cook a minnow supper at the fire.

waiting: No supper yet. The spoon is patient. I am less patient than the spoon.
done: Then it has been tested. I wasn’t there, and the spoon wasn’t there, but it has been tested.
Take the first spoon. I only need the second.

keepsake.name: The first spoon
keepsake.text: Jonas gave it away. He only needs the second.

memories.asked-about-the-second: You asked how the second spoon is different from the first. His answer was “it’s second”. He considers the matter closed.
memories.stamped-also: You guessed the clerk stamped “ALSO” on the form. He had.
memories.suggested-the-ladle: You suggested the third spoon might be a ladle. He has gone quiet and thoughtful.
memories.promised-soup: You promised him a camp stew to test the second spoon on. He wrote it on the spoon.
memories.cooked-the-supper: You cooked a minnow supper so the second spoon could be tested. He wasn’t there. Neither was the spoon.

early: A camp is a lot to ask of a man with two spoons. Give me a reason to put one down.
ask: Your camp has a fire. And a pot. And more than one pair of hands.
That is everything the second spoon requires.
yes: Very well. I’ll bring both spoons. One will be good company.
full: Every bed is taken. I won’t sleep on a spoon. Send word when there is room.
camp.role: Tests every soup with the second spoon.
